input.quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition.
input.rationale: This sits at the fallback: we may assign to an M&A successor without consent, and any other assignment requires consent that cannot be unreasonably withheld. There is no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control. We note the absence of an express affiliate carve-out for us and of any restriction on IBM assigning, which we would raise as a preference rather than a deviation.

input.quote: an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute (internally and externally) copies of, and prepare derivative works based on Type I Materials; and 2. the right to authorize others to do any of the same.
input.rationale: We own Type I Materials and IBM retains its pre-existing Type II Materials with a licence back, which is the right direction. However, for the Materials we own IBM takes an irrevocable, worldwide right to prepare derivative works, distribute them externally and authorise others to do the same — an effectively unlimited give-away of our work product — and the Agreement nowhere confirms that we retain rights in our Content and data. Redline limits IBM's Type I licence to performing the Services and adds a Customer data-ownership sentence. The Enterprise-only scope of the Type II licence (no modification/sublicensing) is noted as a lesser point.
